control.name: CONTROL — stop refusing an SSH push url under a bot identity (the whole fault: the push goes out under a human's key while the commits read as the App's)

mutations.name: quote remote.<name>.url and ignore pushurl (the refusal then names the fetch url that `remote -v`'s first line shows, not the pushurl key that actually carries the SSH value)
mutations.old:
key := "remote." + remote + ".pushurl"
	configured := cfg[key]
	explicitPush := len(configured) > 0
	if !explicitPush {
		key = "remote." + remote + ".url"
		configured = cfg[key]
	}
mutations.new:
key := "remote." + remote + ".url"
	configured := cfg[key]
	explicitPush := false

mutations.name: check only the FIRST push url (a push fans out to every pushurl, so a clean first value is not a pass)
round a failed git-config read up to a pass (could-not-check reported as 'no SSH found, carry on')
round a remote with NO url at all up to a pass (nothing was examined, so nothing can have been cleared)
treat the scp-like `git@host:path` shorthand as not-SSH (the spelling every house checkout actually carries)
swallow the https-without-an-App-credential-helper NOTICE (the ambient-identity shape one layer along, reported as silence)
swallow the unresolvable-$DESK_LOOP NOTICE by making the gate speak for every session (over-application: a human with no App identity is gated too)
decide from the CONFIGURED push url instead of git's resolved one (#884: an https url that url.<base>.insteadOf / pushInsteadOf rewrites to SSH passes)
fall back to the configured url when no push-url resolver is wired (a caller that forgets the resolver silently reinstates #884)
round a failed push-url resolve into the no-url could-not-check (same exit code, wrong story: the operator is sent to configure a remote that is configured)

mutations.name: stop attributing a pushInsteadOf rewrite
give an insteadOf refusal the pushInsteadOf remedy wording (it tells the operator the pushurl escapes because pushInsteadOf never applies to one — the wrong rule kind for an insteadOf refusal)
mutations.old: return rewriteTrace{ruleKey: "url." + base + ".insteadOf", prefix: prefix, from: c}
mutations.new: return rewriteTrace{ruleKey: "url." + base + ".insteadOf", prefix: prefix, from: c, push: true}

mutations.name: deskpr create no longer runs the push-transport gate (the wiring, not the gate: a correct gate nobody calls)
deskpr update no longer runs the push-transport gate
deskwt add no longer runs the push-transport gate (every worktree it cuts inherits the SSH remote unchallenged)
deskpr wires no push-url resolver (the gate then cannot see git's resolved url)
deskwt wires no push-url resolver

the remedy says remove-the-rule for every rewrite, whatever the https target (the SSH-to-SSH insteadOf regression: a set-url remedy that would work is called useless, and removing the rule leaves the SSH url)
the remedy never checks whether insteadOf rewrites the proposed https target back to SSH (it proposes a set-url --push that leaves the refusal standing)

mutations.name: deskwt reads only the FIRST push url (drops --all: a clean first pushurl hides an SSH second one, and `deskwt add` without --role cuts a worktree that pushes to both)
a remote with no url resolved by real git to its bare NAME passes (drops the no-configured-url + [remote] condition: exit 0 where it is could-not-check)
the no-url check ignores the configured value (a url configured as a local path spelled like the remote name is refused as could-not-check)
the insteadOf-rule remedy always claims removing the rule is enough (a pushInsteadOf alias, or an SSH configured url, still sends the push over SSH: two rounds)
a pushInsteadOf-attributed refusal counts the insteadOf rule removal as the whole remedy (drops !rw.push)
the set-url remedy ignores a multi-valued pushurl (prints the plain form git refuses with "has multiple values")
